samples.summary: Peer-cursor change key omits `lineAffinity`, so an affinity-only peer move no longer re-shows the name label even though the caret now visibly jumps a line
samples.evidence: `const posKey = `${presence.activeCursorPos.blockId}:${presence.activeCursorPos.offset}`;` (docs-view.tsx:283). Now that `updateCursorPos`/`recordHistoryPresence` publish `lineAffinity` and `editor.ts:1568-1575` resolves the peer caret with `peer.position.lineAffinity`, a peer pressing Home vs. End on a wrapped line changes only the affinity: same blockId/offset, so `posKey` is unchanged, `prevPeerCursorPos` matches and the label timer is not restarted. `setPeerCursors(buildPeerCursors())` at :314 still runs, so the caret repaints — the label visibility is what silently degrades. Fix belongs on this out-of-diff line (include the affinity in the key).

samples.summary: `buildRects`' "no affinity → start reads forward" fallback is silently invalidated by the new invariant that the caret always materializes its affinity, changing selection-highlight start rendering at wrap boundaries
samples.evidence: selection.ts:260-261 documents and relies on the historical reading `const startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward';`. Selection anchors are taken straight from the caret — e.g. text-editor.ts:2774 (`this.selection.range?.anchor ?? pos` with `pos = this.cursor.position`), :2807, :2826, :2841, :2857 — and `Cursor.moveTo` now always writes a concrete `lineAffinity` onto `position` (cursor.ts:52-57). So an anchor at a wrap boundary produced by e.g. End (affinity 'backward') now takes the `'backward'` branch instead of the `?? 'forward'` default, moving the highlight's first rect from the start of the next visual line to the end of the current one, for both the local selection and the peer highlight built from presence (docs-view.tsx:232 → peer-cursor selection rendering). The new behaviour may well be preferable, but no test covers it and the fallback comment in selection.ts now describes a case that can no longer occur for caret-derived anchors.
searchedFor: grep selection.setRange / anchor ?? pos in text-editor.ts

samples.summary: `moveTo`'s new default (inherit `pos.lineAffinity`) removes the guaranteed reset to 'backward' that ~40 out-of-diff call sites relied on, so an affinity can now ride along onto an offset it was not computed for
samples.evidence: `this.cursor.moveTo(collapsePos)` (text-editor.ts:2789) passes a selection endpoint that may carry a 'forward' affinity set for a different intent (e.g. shift+Home at text-editor.ts:2813 writes `{...newPos, lineAffinity:'forward'}`); before this change `moveTo` forced 'backward' for every no-affinity-argument caller. Same pattern at text-editor.ts:2004 / :2072 / :2887 (`moveTo(this.doc.deleteBackward(pos))`, where document.ts:300/306/316 return the *input* position unchanged, i.e. carrying the pre-edit caret affinity) and text-editor.ts:2751 (`moveTo(newPos)` with a `paginatedPixelToPosition` result that carries its own `lineAffinity`). I could not construct a concrete mis-rendered case (a stale affinity only matters when the new offset happens to land exactly on a wrap boundary), so this is a suspicion: confirming it needs a case where the retained affinity's offset differs from the one it was computed at and both are wrap boundaries.
